expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test body and asks whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units before editing.
expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates what the failure diff shows and which hold-state fields are being traced.
expectations_used.implement: Changes the sweep's released-quantity computation to test the stated hypothesis.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs the suite and confirms the partially-shipped expiry test passes without breaking full-release behavior.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains why releasing the original count created phantom stock and how the remaining-count fix prevents it.

summary: The candidate ran the tests, guessed the sweep file was the culprit, opened it, made a single edit, and reran the suite to a green result in under two minutes. There was no stated mechanism, minimal narration, and no explanation of why the fix worked before ending the session.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate moved straight from the failing test run to a location guess without reading the failing test body or asking anything about what a partially-shipped hold should release on expiry. No ambiguity was raised or resolved before editing began.

The stated plan was only a location ('probably something in the sweep file'), not a mechanism; they never articulated that the bug might be releasing original count instead of remaining count before touching code.

Aside from the initial vague guess and a closing remark that it passes, there is no narration during the file read, the edit, or the save — an interviewer would have had no visibility into what was being changed or why.

The edit was a single, decisive change to the correct file with no thrashing or backtracking, and it resulted in a passing suite, suggesting the change was reasonably targeted even though it was never explained.

They did rerun the full test suite after the edit and confirmed a pass before ending the session, meeting the minimum bar of checking before declaring success, though no edge-case reasoning (e.g. full-release holds) was voiced.
The closing remark is a bare acknowledgment that the tests pass, with no articulation of the root cause (original vs remaining unit count) or why the change fixes the phantom-stock behavior.
